method: Bounded Family landscapes; existing canonical ontology sources reused and deep sources PubMed-verified.

ENV-F01.constructs: Proximity, travel distance, route directness, connectivity, land-use mix and remoteness are distinct objective properties.
ENV-F01.mechanisms: Spatial configuration can constrain route choice and opportunity without determining use.
ENV-F01.operations: Infrastructure or access changes are usually natural experiments rather than blinded manipulations.
ENV-F01.measurement: GIS exposure, network distance and realized travel differ.
ENV-F01.boundaries: Accessibility is not utilization; proximity is not a Social relationship.

ENV-F02.constructs: Walking, cycling, transit, parking, traffic, speed, congestion and route redundancy describe different transport conditions.
ENV-F02.mechanisms: Infrastructure changes opportunity and safety while travel behavior depends on uptake.
ENV-F02.operations: Built-environment natural experiments have selection and concurrent-policy limits.
ENV-F02.measurement: Objective infrastructure, perceived safety and observed use require separate measures.
ENV-F02.boundaries: A facility's presence does not establish exposure or behavior.

ENV-F03.constructs: Layout, sightline, entrance/exit, circulation, seating, enclosure and openness are physical configuration properties.
ENV-F03.mechanisms: Configuration can affect visibility and movement paths.
ENV-F03.operations: Room redesigns typically alter several components together.
ENV-F03.measurement: Geometry and subjective openness/privacy are different levels.
ENV-F03.boundaries: Package redesign cannot identify one component effect.

ENV-F04.constructs: Landmarks, signage, legibility, option visibility, proximity, availability and barriers are distinct.
ENV-F04.mechanisms: Information and geometry can support navigation conditional on perception and ability.
ENV-F04.operations: Signage placement is a message/environment operation, not attention itself.
ENV-F04.measurement: Objective visibility differs from noticed or understood guidance.
ENV-F04.boundaries: Barrier-free design may moderate disability constraints but does not guarantee use.

ENV-F05.constructs: Objective density, physical proximity, privacy, bottlenecks and queues differ from perceived crowding.
ENV-F05.mechanisms: Occupancy and flow constraints can alter movement and exposure.
ENV-F05.operations: Density manipulations often co-vary with noise, delay and interaction.
ENV-F05.measurement: Persons per area is not subjective crowding or stress.
ENV-F05.boundaries: Physical proximity does not entail cohesion, trust or interaction.

ENV-F06.constructs: Ambient level, intermittency, intelligibility, vibration, illuminance, spectrum, daylight, glare and clutter require exact physical specification.
ENV-F06.mechanisms: Acoustic and optical exposures depend on dose, timing, spectrum and task.
ENV-F06.operations: Noise playback and controlled lighting are plausible operations.
ENV-F06.measurement: Objective exposure must be separated from annoyance, attention and performance.
ENV-F06.boundaries: Noise evidence varies by source, task and population; bright-light identity is already governed in BIO-F01.

ENV-F07.constructs: Heat, cold, humidity, wind, precipitation, weather, daylight duration, variability and radiant load differ.
ENV-F07.mechanisms: Achieved physiological strain depends on dose, clothing, activity, acclimation and baseline.
ENV-F07.operations: Climate-chamber exposure can isolate selected factors; field weather cannot.
ENV-F07.measurement: Temperature is not thermal comfort or body strain.
ENV-F07.boundaries: Thermal-cognitive response is task-, dose- and time-dependent.

ENV-F08.constructs: Ventilation, CO2, particulates, gases, VOCs, radiation, pathogens, water contaminants, dampness, mould, odor and cleanliness are distinct.
ENV-F08.mechanisms: Ventilation can alter several indoor contaminants simultaneously.
ENV-F08.operations: Controlled chambers may vary CO2 alone or bundled ventilation/chemical conditions.
ENV-F08.measurement: Room concentration is not personal dose received.
ENV-F08.boundaries: Ventilation/productivity evidence mixes school and office tasks and bundled exposures.

ENV-F09.constructs: Green availability, accessibility, quality, canopy, views, blue space, biodiversity and realized dose differ.
ENV-F09.mechanisms: Natural-setting exposure may alter immediate affect while exercise, expectation and multisensory packages contribute.
ENV-F09.operations: Matched walking-route experiments are plausible but cannot isolate each green component.
ENV-F09.measurement: Availability/accessibility are not realized exposure; affect is not cognition.
ENV-F09.boundaries: Affective findings are more consistent than cognitive transfer and remain heterogeneous.

ENV-F10.constructs: Slope, ruggedness, oxygen availability and water-barrier permeability are physical constraints.
ENV-F10.mechanisms: Terrain can change effort and route feasibility; oxygen exposure differs from achieved physiology.
ENV-F10.operations: Field terrain packages are difficult to isolate.
ENV-F10.measurement: Terrain is not physical capacity; oxygen availability is not tissue oxygenation.
ENV-F10.boundaries: No exact novel operation-to-Driver route survived preliminary triage.

ENV-F11.constructs: Illumination, observability, access control, hazards, exits, shelter, flood, wildfire and structural integrity differ.
ENV-F11.mechanisms: Physical hazard and egress conditions constrain safety responses.
ENV-F11.operations: Hazard simulations often bundle information, urgency and physical constraints.
ENV-F11.measurement: Hazard presence is not perceived risk; shelter availability is not use.
ENV-F11.boundaries: No broad hazard-to-psychology causal claim is inferred.

ENV-F12.constructs: Food, water, sanitation, housing, tools, electricity, fuel, medical material and supply continuity are resource conditions.
ENV-F12.mechanisms: Availability and proximity create opportunity conditional on access and uptake.
ENV-F12.operations: Resource provision packages mix physical and institutional changes.
ENV-F12.measurement: Availability is not consumption or benefit.
ENV-F12.boundaries: Existing cross-Layer water and supply reviews are reused.

ENV-F13.constructs: Infrastructure functionality, blockage, debris and utility redundancy concern system condition.
ENV-F13.mechanisms: Damage and redundancy can affect continuity through network-specific mechanisms.
ENV-F13.operations: Infrastructure restoration is a package rather than one universal component.
ENV-F13.boundaries: No new Network State or derived environmental variable is required.
